subject.title: Feature Request: Disable exec command credential masking / secret replacement

question: Should OpenClaw add any trusted opt-out for forced tool/exec safety-boundary redaction, and if so should it be display-only, per-run/per-agent, or not accepted?
rationale: The current code intentionally keeps UI/tool/approval redaction independent from general logging redaction, and changing that boundary can expose credentials across multiple surfaces; automation cannot choose the acceptable threat model.

options.title: Keep forced safety redaction
options.body: Leave tool, approval, diagnostics, Gateway, and UI redaction forced while asking for a concrete live repro if shell execution itself is being mutated.

options.title: Design a narrow trusted escape hatch
options.body: Approve a tightly scoped opt-out, such as a display-only parser exemption or explicit trusted run mode, with tests proving default redaction still holds.

options.title: Allow broad credentialGuard false
options.body: Accept a global or per-agent config knob that can disable safety-boundary masking, with clear documentation of credential exposure risk.

recommendation.title: Keep forced safety redaction
recommendation.body: Leave tool, approval, diagnostics, Gateway, and UI redaction forced while asking for a concrete live repro if shell execution itself is being mutated.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across security defaults, config surface policy, exec approvals, and logging behavior where recent history points to this owner path.
